summary: Grays Harbor County: a 1940 two-story cabin, a 1957 40-foot DNR tower gone by 1970, and a logged summit where a timber company's permit is needed.

facts.design: Two-story 10x10 ft cabin (1940), then a 40 ft wooden live-in tower (1957)
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1970. A 2000 visit found one footing and an eyebolt; a 2016 visit found no footings.

access.note: Private timber land. As of 2016 Weyerhaeuser required a permit for anyone to enter the area; a cheaper general access permit allows off-season visits from February 1 to July 31.

visit.trail_note: Willhite's route is about 3.6 miles from a gate on the Black Creek road, with about 700 feet of gain, and a permit is needed. No tower stands to climb.

events.note: Two-story 10x10 cabin, called a smokehouse, built with about three miles of new road as a semi-permanent lookout
Aircraft Warning Service activated the station on March 11, 1942 under the Olympia Filter Center
AWS station used existing state facilities and added a 12 by 20 garage; the State kept the site after service ended
Mrs. Ben Harner operated the lookout that season
Leah Warren of Shelton on duty in June 1955
A 40 ft wooden DNR live-in tower replaced the 1940 cabin
Cleo Wing of Montesano on duty when the new tower went into service in August 1957
Tower gone by 1970 per the register and FireLookout.com; the year it came down is not stated
Visit right after a harvest found at least one footing and an eyebolt
Registered January 19, 2012 as US 1202, WA 103; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com describe a two-story smokehouse for 1940. The 1940 association report quoted on Forest Lookouts calls it a ten-foot square structure. The story uses the two-story description and the ten-foot size they share.
Willhite gives about three miles of new road for 1940; the 1940 report quoted on Forest Lookouts gives three and a quarter miles. The story gives both figures.

sources.title: Prices Peak Lookout Site - Grays Harbor County

notes_for_editor: The 1940 to 1970 timeline is consistent across four sources. Access (permission, 2016 permit rule) rests on a 2016 trip report; check Weyerhaeuser's current permit terms before any visit. A 1952 item in The Daily Chronicle, as quoted on Forest Lookouts, spells the lookout Price Creek and says Betty Harner tended it; it is not used because the match to this site is not clear. No staffing after 1957 was found in the sources read. No new photos were added. Used 1 WebSearch and about 7 page reads, counting repeat reads of the same pages. Fact-check 2026-10-09: Willhite's 1953 and 1962 survey notes suggest a 90-foot tower may have stood before the 1957 tower, so the story calls 1940 the earliest dated lookout rather than the first.
